meta.title: What Shall We Wear?
meta.textType: dialogue: new words from a set

paragraphs: On Thursday, Teacher Kim told the class about a short opera. On Friday, the class had to perform it for the little children. After the practice, she gave everybody a note about the clothes. The note said, "Be dressed in a white blouse or shirt and dark trousers or a dark skirt." It also said, "Bring a hoodie, a backpack, and a small purse." The last line said, "Wear black school shoes."

At the library table, Leo read the note and made a face. "What is a blouse?" he asked. "It is a shirt for a girl or a woman," said May. "You can wear your white shirt, because you are a boy." "And dressed means that you have your clothes on," said Lily. "We must be dressed in white and dark colors." "I understand now," said Leo. "Can I wear my football shorts?" he asked with a smile. "No!" said everybody. Then everybody laughed, and Leo laughed the most.

"What is a hoodie?" asked Mia. "I think it is a warm jacket with a hood," said Leo. "A hood is the part that covers your head." "Yes, and it is cold in the school hall," said May. "We need hoodies, especially in the morning." "But the opera is in the afternoon," said Lily. "Then we put the hoodies in our backpacks," said Mia. "A backpack is a bag that you carry on your back."

"What is a purse?" asked Leo. "It is a small bag for money," said May. "Why do we need money?" asked Leo. "The bus costs money, and we want a cold drink afterwards," said Lily. "My purse is red," said Mia, "and my backpack is blue." "I will put my football in my backpack," said Leo. "We can play after the show." "Then I will bring my football, too," said May. "We can make two teams on the field."

Teacher Kim came to the table and listened. "You are very good at new words," she said. "The words blouse, hoodie, purse, and backpack are all things that you wear or carry." "So you can guess what they mean from the set." "Please check your clothes tonight," she said. "Tomorrow, you perform for the little children." Lily wrote the four new words in her notebook, and she drew a small picture next to each one.
